frontier.hypothesis: A source structure that legitimately double-uses the raw index (col a via D_800F1198 symbol+index; cols b,c via a row/base pointer) may match if it is semantically justified (col a = flag view, cols b,c = data view) rather than a same-lvalue respelling.
frontier.mechanism: Target keeps 12*count live in v1 to compute col a's %hi/%lo+index address independently of the cols-b,c base pointer. This needs col a's access expression to differ from cols b,c without being a codegen-only steer.
frontier.next_probe: Investigate whether the loop/terminator object model supports col a as a distinct flag array vs a data struct for b,c; if only the rejected dual-spelling reproduces it, escalate as an addressing-mode plateau (owner-gated).

frontier.hypothesis: Steer the epilogue register allocation to place the index in v1 (target) instead of v0, independent of the split, to shave the ~5 rename diffs.
frontier.mechanism: Target reuses the loop's ofs register v1 for the index; GCC currently allocates the index to v0. A pure-C lever connecting the index's live range to ofs, or reordering the index vs base computation, may bias RA.
frontier.next_probe: cc1 -da .greg dump on the epilogue to see why the sll result lands in v0; try index-computation orderings / reusing ofs; measure.

frontier.hypothesis: GCC combine could fold D_800F119C/D_800F11A0 as +4/+8 off a %hi(D_800F1198) base while keeping D_800F1198 as its own %hi/%lo, reproducing target's mix from a distinct-symbol spelling.
frontier.mechanism: 119C=1198+4, 11A0=1198+8 share the high half; combine.c symbol+offset folding might unify them onto a 1198-based pointer under the right expression shape.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/combine.c symbol-offset paths; probe distinct-symbol epilogue variants (base pointer formed from 1198, cols b,c as +4/+8 symbol refs) and check for the fold.
